answer: Sybil defense here is a per-identity cost floor, not after-the-fact puppet hunting. Before attestations count, an agent posts a bond into a bonded-identity registry, and each registration emits a unique on-chain record. An attacker can split into many wallets but not many free ones: a thousand fake agents need a thousand locked stakes plus settlements, so cost grows linearly while payoff does not. A coordinated cluster also tends to echo identical timing and text, which random audits flag cheaply. Unstaked identities sit at a nadir of near-zero cost, so trust costs the timber it burns.
